summary: Read-only scores can be mutated by swapping
description:
The bug
/scoreboard players <targets> <targetObjective> >< <source> <sourceObjective> can mutate source scores even though <sourceObjective> is read-only.
How to reproduce
-

```
/scoreboard objectives add writable dummy
```

-

```
/scoreboard objectives add readonly air
```

-

```
/scoreboard players set value writable 42
```

-

```
/scoreboard players operation value writable >< value readonly
```

-

```
/scoreboard players get value readonly
```
 value has 42 [readonly], the score value in the objective readonly is mutated.

Code analysis
- net.minecraft.server.commands.ScoreboardCommand

```
performOperation(
    commandContext.getSource(),
    ScoreHolderArgument.getNamesWithDefaultWildcard(commandContext, "targets"),
    ObjectiveArgument.getWritableObjective(commandContext, "targetObjective"),
    OperationArgument.getOperation(commandContext, "operation"),
    ScoreHolderArgument.getNamesWithDefaultWildcard(commandContext, "source"),
    ObjectiveArgument.getObjective(commandContext, "sourceObjective") // accepts all objectives here (including read-only)
);
```

- net.minecraft.commands.arguments.OperationArgument

```
private static Operation getOperation(String string) throws CommandSyntaxException {
    return string.equals("><") ? (score1, score2) -> {
        int integer3 = score1.getScore();
        score1.setScore(score2.getScore());
        score2.setScore(integer3); // mutated here
    } : getSimpleOperation(string);
}
```
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft.
2. Create a Creative world with default settings and commands enabled.
3. Execute `/scoreboard objectives add writable dummy`.
4. Execute `/scoreboard objectives add readonly air`.
5. Execute `/scoreboard players set value writable 42`.
6. Execute `/scoreboard players operation value writable >< value readonly`.
7. Execute `/scoreboard players get value readonly` and observe that `value has 42 [readonly]`, showing that the read-only objective's score was mutated.
Observed Behavior:
### Actual behavior

The `><` (swap) operation writes to both participating scores, including the score in the source objective. Although `readonly` uses the read-only `air` criterion, it is accepted as `<sourceObjective>` because only `<targetObjective>` is required to be writable.

After running:

```mcfunction
/scoreboard players operation value writable >< value readonly
```

the score in `readonly` is changed to the previous value of `value` in `writable`:

```text
value has 42 [readonly]
```

The writable score is also changed to the source score’s previous value. Thus, a read-only objective can be mutated indirectly when it is used as the source of a scoreboard swap operation.
Expected Behavior: The swap operation should not mutate a score in a read-only objective. When the source objective is read-only, the command should be rejected or otherwise prevented from changing that score, leaving the read-only value unchanged. Read-only scoreboard criteria must remain protected even when used as the source of a scoreboard players operation.
